render.tilesManifestPrelude:
# os2warp (VMID 108) — *** TCG ONLY *** (OS/2 Warp 4 will NOT boot under KVM).
#   pc,acpi=off,usb=off, -cpu pentium, std VGA, sb16, pcnet NIC, PS/2. VERBATIM
#   LAUNCHER: COM1 serial chardev (serial.sock) + conditional -loadvm golden
#   (no -snapshot — savevm/loadvm persist; the OS/2 register nag never returns).
# DISPLAY: Warp 4.52 (MCP2) + IBM GENGRADD at 1024x768x64k on -vga std.
#   -global VGA.vgamem_mb=2 is LOAD-BEARING: GENPMI's mode tables hold 64 VESA
#   modes and SeaVGABIOS reports 93 at the 16 MB default, overflowing them
#   (trap c0000005 at display init). 2 MB trims the list to 46. See
#   docs/guests/os2warp.md.
# POINTER: in-guest warpd agent (guest-agents/os2/warpd_os2.c -> C:\WARPD.EXE,
#   PM WinSetPointerPos, Y-flipped) over COM1. Critical enablers: DosDevIOCtl
#   SET_DCBINFO forcing MODE_NOWAIT_READ_TIMEOUT, a PM message queue, and
#   MouSetPtrPos mirroring each warp into OS/2's native mouse subsystem. Buttons
#   ride the real QEMU PS/2 device (--warpd-buttons qemu) for PM capture, frame
#   sizing, menus, and double-clicks; the 80ms guard orders serial motion first.
render.tilesManifestInvocation:
emit os2warp \
  --tile os2warp --vmid 108 --udp 54108 --pointer warpd \
  --warpd-addr unix:/data/vms/streamhost/tiles/os2warp/serial.sock \
  --warpd-buttons qemu --warpd-wheel agent --warpd-pace-ms 8 \
  --warpd-button-delay-ms 80 --audio on --fps 30 \
  --launcher-file "$T/os2warp/qemu-streamhost.sh"
